core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 12712-12719): for a point x with strict henselization O^sh_{X,x}, the henselization is a normal domain by the algebra lemma, so Spec(K) x_X Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) is irreducible; the stalk description of the pushforward then gives (g_*underline E)_{xbar} = E, so g_*underline E = underline E.

Part (2) (proof lines 12721-12728): since g factors through j there is a map j_*underline E -> g_*underline E, which is injective because for every V etale over X the scheme Spec(K) x_X V is dense in U x_X V; combined with the canonical map underline E -> j_*underline E this gives the identification j_*underline E = underline E.
proof_roadmap: Show the base change of the generic point along a strict henselization is irreducible and read off the stalk of g_* of the constant sheaf.
Compare j_*underline E with g_*underline E through the factorisation of g and the density of the generic fibre to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that on an integral normal scheme the pushforward of a constant sheaf along either the inclusion of the generic point or the inclusion of a nonempty open is again the constant sheaf (statement lines 12699-12709). The proof (proof lines 12711-12728) computes the stalks of g_*underline E using the normality of strict henselizations and the stalk description of pushforwards, and then deduces the statement for an open immersion from the factorisation g = j o (generic point of U) together with the density of the generic fibre over etale neighbourhoods. H2: one stalk computation plus one comparison, written out.
